title: state-reconciliation-and-healing-playbook-2026
author: Asha Menon
body:
Overview
========

Purpose
-------
This playbook defines the standard approach Redwood teams should use to detect, reconcile, and heal divergent service state across the inference platform. It covers causal classes of state divergence (cache drift, metadata mismatch, KV-staleness, session affinity splits), detection signals, automatic and manual reconciliation patterns, test and rollout guidance, and ownership. The goal is to minimize customer-visible disruption while keeping reconciliation fast, auditable, and safe for multi-tenant production environments.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: control plane metadata, runtime KV caches (prefix/KV caches), model variant manifests, routing tables, and tenant-scoped leases. Does not cover long-term archival storage (S3) or external customer DBs.
- Audience: runtime engineers, SRE, platform, on-call responders, and private-deployment operators.

Definitions
-----------
- Divergence: any observable difference between two authoritative representations of the same logical state (e.g., control-plane manifest vs runtime cache).
- Repair action: a reconciliation operation that modifies one or more systems to restore a single canonical view.
- Escalation threshold: a metric threshold that triggers human intervention.

Principles
----------
1. Authoritativeness: for each domain, a single system is the canonical authority (e.g., Control Plane = model manifest source of truth; KV Coordinator = cache lease owner).
2. Observability-first: every reconciliation must be accompanied by telemetry (pre/post snapshots, diffs, and event IDs).
3. Safe-by-default: automatic heals must be idempotent, rate-limited, and reversible where possible.
4. Tenant safety: reconciliation must never leak data between tenants and must respect confidentiality settings.
5. Auditability: all automated repairs produce an immutable audit event with a UUID and optional human comment.

Signal catalogue (what we monitor)
----------------------------------
- Telemetry signals (primary):
  - DivergenceCount: per-tenant counter of detected mismatches (threshold default: 5 in 10m).
  - KV-eviction-rate spikes when compared to manifest-change-rate (>3x baseline).
  - SessionAffinityBreaks: number of requests where session cookies indicate conflicting routing (>1% of traffic for 5m).
  - ManifestChecksumMismatch: control-plane vs runtime checksum drift (>0.5% of models loaded).
  - RepairFailures: automated repair attempts that return non-2xx.
- Alerts derived from signals (default thresholds):
  - P1: ManifestChecksumMismatch > 2% tenants OR DivergenceCount surge > 100/s globally.
  - P2: DivergenceCount > 5 for >10m for any tenant.
  - P3: RepairFailures > 10% for a reconciliation job.

Reconciliation patterns (catalog)
--------------------------------
1. Sidecar Resync (automatic, low-risk)
   - Purpose: push authoritative manifest to runtime sidecars and accept their ACK.
   - Safe conditions: when manifest delta is only additive (new annotations) and tenant not in maintenance window.
   - Rate-limits: 50 sidecars/s global by default.
   - Observability: capture pre/post checksums, per-sidecar latency and ack status.

2. Lazy Repair (automatic, medium-risk)
   - Purpose: schedule background repair of stale KV entries using coordinated compare-and-swap from the KV coordinator.
   - Safe conditions: repair only keys with TTL < 24h and when interception rate < 0.1% per shard.
   - Backoff strategy: exponential with jitter (base=5s, cap=10m).

3. Canary Roll-forward (automatic/manual, higher-risk)
   - Purpose: when major manifest rewrite required, apply to canary tenants then roll forward with rollback on SLO regression.
   - Safety gates: synthetic evaluation harness pass, latency SLO within 5% of baseline, failure rate <0.1%.

4. Manual Arbitration (human-in-loop)
   - Purpose: for complex or data-destructive conflicts (lease contests, contradictory model signatures).
   - Steps: collect diffs, snapshot impacted runtimes, create a repair ticket with recommended authoritative action, and obtain approvals from owner_team.

5. Shadow Reconcile (dry-run)
   - Purpose: validate a reconciliation plan by simulating state changes in a shadow environment and producing metrics without committing.

Operational runbook: common play paths
--------------------------------------
A. Automatic repair path (triggered by DivergenceCount threshold)
1. Event is detected by the Reconciliation Detector service (svc: state-reconciler).
2. The detector emits a ReconciliationIntent with UUID and attempts Sidecar Resync for affected tenants.
3. If sidecar acks reach 95% within 2m, reconciliation closes automatically and an audit event is written to telemetry-index (trace id included).
4. If sidecar acks < 95% or any RepairFailures observed, escalate to Lazy Repair.
5. If Lazy Repair fails 3 consecutive times for the same tenant, open a P2 incident with owner_team set to runtime-infra.

B. Manual escalation (P1)
1. Pager fires to oncall SRE + runtime tech lead.
2. Oncall runs the Reconciliation Triage checklist (CLI snippet below).
3. Triage coordinator assigns 'repair-owner' and decides between Canary Roll-forward and Manual Arbitration.

Reconciliation triage CLI (example)
-----------------------------------
# Fetch the latest reconciliation intent and diffs
redwoodctl state-reconciler show --intent UUID

# Snapshot runtime state for tenant 'tenant-123' into s3 (read-only)
redwoodctl runtime snapshot --tenant tenant-123 --out s3://redwood-temp/snapshots/tenant-123-$(date +%s).tar.gz

Safeguards and gating rules
---------------------------
- Never auto-delete authoritative artifacts (signed model files, manifests) without an explicit human approval unless TTL has expired and a policy allows it.
- Repairs that change authorization metadata require manual approval from security (owner_team: security).
- All cross-tenant visible reconciliation actions must be run at 02:00–04:00 PT or during approved maintenance windows unless the incident is P1.
- Rollbacks: Every automated change must publish a rollback plan with a duration estimate and a rollback command (included in the audit event).

Telemetry and metrics to emit for each repair attempt
----------------------------------------------------
- reconciliation.intent_id: UUID
- reconciliation.kind: one of [sidecar-resync, lazy-repair, canary-rollforward, manual-arbitration]
- reconciliation.start_ts, reconciliation.end_ts
- reconciliation.success: true|false
- reconciliation.affected_tenants_count
- reconciliation.estimated_cost_tokens (an internal unit used for billing scope)
- pre_checksum, post_checksum (control-plane vs runtime)
- repair_commands_executed (list of command IDs emitted)

Example reconciliation audit event (text)
--------------------------------------
ID: rcon-20260208-9f1b
Owner: runtime-infra
Kind: sidecar-resync
Scope: tenant=tenant-123, sidecars=42
Pre-checksum: abc123
Post-checksum: abc123
Result: success
Note: 38/42 sidecars acked within 90s, four sidecars delayed due to GKE node drain; follow-up job scheduled.

SLOs and acceptable windows
---------------------------
- Detection latency: 95th percentile detection of divergence within 5 minutes of occurrence.
- Automated repair success rate: >= 99% for sidecar-resyncs.
- Mean time to reconcile (MTTR) for P2 incidents: < 30 minutes from ticket creation to resolution in 90% of cases.
- Audit coverage: 100% of repair actions must produce an audit event.

Testing and verification
------------------------
- Synthetic tests: the reconciliation harness (svc: reconcile-harness) must run daily against a staging fleet creating seeded divergences for the following classes: manifest drift, KV TTL expiry, lease takeover.
- Shadow simulation: every major reconciliation change must be shadow-tested in the canary cluster for at least 24 hours and show no increase in tail-latency (>5th percentile) or error-rate.
- Contract tests: control-plane -> runtime reconcile contract tests live in repo: infra/reconcile/contract_tests. These tests must run in CI on any change to state-reconciler, kv-coordinator or manifest-service.

Runbook checklist (for oncall)
------------------------------
1. Acknowledge pager and open incident ticket using the standardized template.
2. Run the triage CLI and attach snapshots to the incident.
3. Determine scope: tenant-specific vs global.
4. If global, notify product and legal if customer-impact > 1% of active tenants.
5. Choose repair pattern and kick off repair job.
6. Monitor reconciliation telemetry; if deviation grows, execute rollback plan and escalate.
7. After resolution, run postmortem template (link to related_pages) and tag SLO exposure.

Ownership and lifecycle
-----------------------
- Primary owner: runtime-infra (contact: runtime-infra@redwood.ai)
- Secondary owner: eng-sre for paging and incident process.
- Policy review cadence: annual review in January; minor updates as required after major incidents.

Related pages and artifacts
---------------------------

- KV coordinator design doc (link: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runtime-architecture/adaptive-kv-coordinator-and-eviction-contract-2026)
- Reconciliation harness repo: git@github.com:redwood/reconcile-harness (internal)

Appendix: sample YAML job for a Sidecar Resync
---------------------------------------------
# This is a human-readable example. The real job is created via the state-reconciler API
job:
  kind: sidecar_resync
  owner: runtime-infra
  tenants: ["tenant-123"]
  rate_limit_per_second: 20
  safe_flags:
    allow_data_write: false
    require_ack_threshold: 0.95
  audit_comment: "Resync after manifest drift detected by reconcile-detector v2"

Audit and post-incident steps
----------------------------
- Every P1/P2 incident with a reconciliation action requires a post-incident review. Include:
  - Timeline of detection -> repair -> resolution.
  - Telemetry diffs and repro steps.
  - Corrective actions and owners.
  - A follow-up scheduled in the policy review cadence.
